You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image visibly present its depicted content as a drawing rather than as an unchanged photograph?
node.criteria: pass: visible rendering establishes a drawing, such as drawn or illustrated forms; fail: the depicted content remains clearly photographic with no visible drawing conversion; unknown: the image does not establish whether it is a drawing or photograph.
node.binding: Assess only whether the image has been rendered as a drawing; do not assess its medium.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image visibly renders the giraffes and surroundings with soft, sketch-like outlines and drawn shading rather than retaining the source photograph’s photographic appearance.

n3: The node’s aggregation rule is too permissive: it treats two passing supports as proof of complete fulfillment, but the edited image still retains strongly photographic giraffe detail and composition despite its chalk-like texture and softened, drawn surroundings. This is evidence of progress, not necessarily a complete transformation. Keep the independent chalk-medium and drawing-form checks, but make the final criterion assess whether the image as a whole has actually become a chalk drawing, rather than equating texture plus sketch-like cues with completion. Preserve partial when evidence supports some requested change but not full fulfillment; do not infer absence from uncertainty or add requirements beyond the instruction. The issue is semantic aggregation, not transport or dependency failure.

response.content: {"text":"The binding currently tests only whether the image reads as a drawing, so it can pass on sketch-like outlines and shading even when the requested chalk treatment is not established. Keep this node focused on drawing form, but make its pass criterion distinguish a convincing whole-image conversion from localized or superficial drawn cues: the edited image shows chalky texture and softened surroundings, yet the giraffes retain substantial photographic detail and the composition remains recognizable as a photo-derived scene. Treat that as evidence of progress, not by itself proof of complete drawing conversion; reserve fail for no visible conversion and unknown for genuinely insufficient evidence. Do not make this node judge chalk medium—that remains an independent check—and do not treat confidence or repeated variation as evidence of absence. The trace has no transport, schema, or dependency failure; the mismatch is semantic calibration of the pass criterion."}
